recipes.name: Shrimp Chowder
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound frozen cooked shrimp, thawed and drained

steps.text: Heat butter in a large soup pot over medium-low heat. Add celery and onions; cook and stir until vegetables are completely softened, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Add cream cheese and milk; stir over low heat until cream cheese is completely melted.
Add potatoes, shrimp, dry white wine and salt. Heat thorough, stirring occasionally; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Chowder
raw_recipe.description: An easy shrimp chowder with cooked potatoes and sautéed onions is enriched with white wine, cream cheese, and milk for a rich and creamy seafood soup.

review.reviewBody:
delicious recipe, great for the cold weather!
I used a half pound of large shrimp and cut them in half. I also added about 2T. parsley to the butter when i sauteed the onions and celery. Because I used about 3 c. diced potatoes, I needed more milk (about an extra 3/4 c.), but the cream cheese kept the mixture thick. One more addition I made was 1T. of old bay. Excellent flavor! Will make again!

1/3/10- I made this again today, a little more gourmet, but both equally as delish!! I made a shrimp stock with the shells (adding old bay), once the stock was finished, I removed the shells and cooked the shrimp then used the stock to cook the potatoes. I added some white wine (maybe a Tbsp) to the onion celery mixure while it was cooking, and added more half and half for more broth. I did add about a half cup of corn niblets for color and because,,, well chowders and corn marry so well!! OH I also added some lobster that was left from new years dinner :) If you haven't made this yet, you really should! Don't be nervous with the amount of cream cheese, it adds such a great, rich flavor! And if its too thick add more milk, half and half, evaporated milk, shrimp stock or whatever you're using for the liquid in your recipe... restaurant quality for sure!!

Yummy! I only made half and added a tbsp of chopped parsley to butter(instead of margarine) as a viewer suggested. I also doubled potatoes (pre- boiled). I had 2 percent milk so added 1/ 2!cup + 6 tbsp whipping cream( just needed to use). I also added 1 tsp old bay. Yum! I didn’t have cooked shrimp so cooked raw in a bit of olive and earlier in the day. We had snow so had to use what I had on hand but this is a great beginner recipe to alter as you see fit! Perfect with a tossed salad and saltines for a cold day! Thank you!

This recipe has some serious flaws:

The recipe doesn't specify that the called-for potatoes need to be cooked before the soup is assembled. They are added just before the soup is warmed for serving. I scurried at the last minute to boil the potatoes 

Also, the "warming" doesn't allow sufficient time for the wine to cook off, leaving a harsh "booziness." 

The recipe also doesn't suggest dicing the shrimp. This is nnot a major issue, and may be a matter of taste.

All that being said, I made the soup, using a half-pound of jumbo shrimp (twelve). I sauteed the raw shrimp (fresh, in my case) (shells on) late in the prepping of the onion/celery mix, thinking this would -- if only slightly -- enhance soup's eventual flavor. I peeled (and diced) the shrimp after they were all but cooked (about five or six minutes) in the vegetable.

The soup is OK. A bit boozy from the uncooked wine. Perhaps the wine should have been added with the sauteing vegetables?

I might make it again....a bit wiser about the details next time.

Lesson learned: always read a recipe closely (process, as well as called-for ingredients) before starting. Mea culpe.

I made some changes and additions. I didn't have celery or white wine so I substituted canned cream of celery soup for the milk & celery, added 3 cups chicken broth to simmer the potatoes in and I didn't peel the mini potatoes because I prefer the taste and nutrition of leaving the skins on, added some sauteed chopped red pepper and baby carrot coins to the sautéed onions & mixed them with sautéed shallots, used a tub of Philadelphia jalapeño cream cheese instead of plain cream cheese to give the chowder a kick and for flavoring, cooked the chowder with 2 bay leaves, mixed peppercorns, paprika, dill and parsley, mixing in 1/4 cup capers and 3 chopped scallions at the last minute. Ambrosia!

Delicious, like everyone says. Picky 4 year-old ate it. Second round modifications: substituted milk for broth, added half cup of corn, Old Bay seasoning, and used up leftover mashed potatoes in place of the cubed potatoes. If you want to thin out chowder: add milk or broth. To thicken, I added potato flakes. Excellent baseline recipe to modify for your family's needs.

We really liked this recipe and the only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 was b/c if I hadn't read other reviews first, I wouldn't have known to cook the potatoes and soften the cream cheese before adding them to avoid frustration and/or burning the milk due to the long melt/cook time. I followed the recipe except for these changes: I omitted the celery & salt and substituted 1/4 tsp of celery salt because I didn't have any celery on hand. I increased the onions to 2/3 cup b/c we like onions. I used Neufchatel cheese in place of the cream cheese and softened it in the microwave before adding it to the stock pot to reduce time needed to melt it. It still took a while to melt, though. I upped the potatoes to 3 cups and boiled them in one can of reduced sodium chicken broth with 1 Tbsp of Old Bay and when the potatoes were fork tender, I added the entire mixture. We had 17 extra large-sized shrimp (which had been steamed with Old Bay) leftover from Christmas, and I cut them into bite sized pieces before adding. I also used 2 cups frozen white corn (b/c I can't imagine chowder without corn), 1 extra Tbsp Old Bay (we're from MD and love our Old Bay!), and 1/4 tsp white pepper. This made 6 cereal-sized bowls of soup. I was full after one bowl, but my husband ate THREE because he thought it was so good! This could easily make a meal if served with salad and/or crusty bread. Or as another reviewer suggested, serve it in a bread bowl. Thanks for a great starter recipe!

Pretty good stuff! The whole family liked it.

I used red potatoes and boiled them in chicken broth, old bay and creole seasoning. I then sauteed the celery and onions with a little old bay and creole. I added some frozen corn and all other ingredients as stated.

I added some additional old bay and creole to taste and it was fabulous!

This also doubles as a REALLY good chicken corn chowder if you add the corn. Just cube up your chicken and fry it. Then make the recipie with chicken. Yummy!

I read all the reviews on this chowder and then combined the suggestions as follows (I doubled the recipe BTW): Precooked the potatoes in 2 cans of chicken broth and reserved the cooking liquid, Added 1 Tbsp. minced garlic and 2 Tbsp. of dried parsley flakes when I sauted the celery after omitting the onions (picky eaters), warmed up the cream cheese in micro in order to speed up the melting in the soup pot, added a few drops of Tabasco sauce and a bay leaf, added 2 cups slightly defrosted frozen whole kernel corn with shrimp and omitted the wine. After adding the shrimp, corn, salt and pepper; the chowder was a little too thick so I added 2 cups of the reserved chicken broth from the potatoes. Next time I'll add a half cup at a time until the desired thickness is reached; it ended just a little too thin for my tastes. Anyway, after alll these changes my family was happily surprised with this dish. Don't know if I'll make it again though:)

Love this recipe! I turned it into an easy crock pot meal as these tend to fit my lifestyle better. As for ingredients I increased the milk to 1 & 3/4 cup like other reviewers, instead of salt I used seasoning salt, added 1 TBSP of Old Bay seasoning and 3/4 of an 11 oz can of super sweet yellow and white corn. Basically I just melted the cream cheese, milk, and margarine in a medium saucepan. Added all of the other ingredients into the crock pot with my additions and poured the melted cream cheese mixture over and cooked on low 6-8 hours. This really simplified the recipe for me!

Delicious starter recipe! I sautéed the onion, celery and 1/2 a chopped red pepper in a teaspoon of coconut oil. I added 4oz cream cheese, 8oz evaporated milk, 4oz almond milk and 8oz chicken broth. I then chose to add 1 precooked chopped sweet potato, 1 can creamed corn and 1/2 cup frozen corn. I cooked the shrimp in a tsp of coconut oil and added it last. I seasoned it with 1 tsp creole seasoning, dried parsley, oregano and a dash of red pepper. WOW!!!

Very good! Per other reviews, I cooked the potatoes first in vegetable broth. Reserved 1 cup of broth to add to soup. Used skim milk and lowfat cream cheese.(trying to save calories and fat). Added 1 T old bay seasoning. Used 2 cups of potatoes and 12 oz of shrimp. Serves 4 very small portions.
For the 1X recipe, I added 1 C frozen corn kernels, 1/2 tsp Old Bay seasoning, 1/4 tsp ground cayenne and a few sliced garlic cloves. I like it!
it was delicious

I used frozen tail on raw Argentine shrimp, thawed and removed tails. Cut into bite size pieces to compensate for being uncooked. Rest of recipe as original. LOVED that quantity was for 4 servings, it’s just the 2 of us. My husband ate 3, and begged me to make again soon. Quadrupled for Foodie club; I had nothing to take home.
Had to add a few of my own spices. Turned out great.
totally inedible. Tastes NOTHING like any sort of chowder should. So much cream cheese, it ruined it.
Way too much cream cheese. Will make a roux add milk for regular cream soup and pullout all the shrimp:potatoes and a bit of cream cheese. My husband liked it more than I did

This is absolutely delicious. Initially, the recipe confused me because it did not specify to boil the diced potatoes. However, I knew better. I easily doubled the recipe. I added parsley, & garlic with the butter & red onions. Sautéed them in butter. I used half & half. The cream cheese with the half & half reduced down easily smooth. I cut the shrimp in half because I prefer smaller bites. I served it with a box of Red Lobster Cheddar Cheese biscuits. What a great gloomy day meal.
This recipe would be better if the base was doubled. Same veggies. Double cream cheese & milk. Maybe even a bit of chicken or seafood broth.
Excellent. I doubled it added Sherry, Old Bay, and Parsley. pre boiled potatoes in seafood broth and added more onions. A couple of my tweaks to an excellent recipe! Thank you for sharing!
